with src as (
    select
        p.payment_id,
        p.order_id,
        p.paid_amount,
        p.paid_date,
        o.amount
    from {{ source('legacy', 'payments') }} p
    join {{ source('legacy', 'orders') }} o
        on o.order_id = p.order_id
),
running as (
    select
        payment_id,
        order_id,
        paid_amount,
        amount,
        sum(paid_amount) over (
            partition by order_id
            order by paid_date nulls first, payment_id nulls first
            rows between unbounded preceding and current row
        ) as raw_running_sum,
        sum(case when paid_amount is null then 1 else 0 end) over (
            partition by order_id
            order by paid_date nulls first, payment_id nulls first
            rows between unbounded preceding and current row
        ) as null_paids_seen
    from src
),
final as (
    select
        payment_id,
        order_id,
        cast(paid_amount as decimal(18,2)) as paid_amount,
        case
            when null_paids_seen > 0 then cast(null as decimal(18,2))
            else cast(raw_running_sum as decimal(18,2))
        end as cumulative_paid,
        amount
    from running
)
select
    payment_id,
    order_id,
    paid_amount,
    cumulative_paid,
    cast(amount - cumulative_paid as decimal(18,2)) as balance_after,
    case when cumulative_paid > amount then 1 else 0 end as overpaid
from final

explanation: This procedure builds a payment ledger that tracks how much has been paid against each order. Payments are processed in date order within each order, and each row shows the running total paid, the remaining balance, and whether the order has been overpaid. The set-based version uses a window sum partitioned by order, which gives the same running totals as the cursor loop.
